info.description: Enterprise-grade E2E Postman Suite for the IT Patch Registry Service Domain (BIAN-aligned, ADR-001/005/013/019/030/031/032/033). Creates a patch policy (days allowed for a critical, high, medium and low patch), reads and lists it, reports a fresh patch within its deadline, the same patch again (200, the stored finding, what was reported again changes nothing) and a critical patch already past its deadline, and shows how the policy judges itself when read: COMPLIANT with one open patch within time, OVERDUE with the deadline that was missed, a waiver in force taking the patch out of the count, the waiver withdrawn, the patch applied and the policy COMPLIANT again, an applied patch never reopened by a repeated report. It updates the definition, pauses and resumes the policy, lists findings newest announcement first with filters and a limit, and reads both audit ledgers in order. A second folder proves the registry is staff only (a REQUESTER gets 403 ERR-PCH-00403 on every route). A third covers the negative guarantees: validation (blank or long name, missing asset, days out of range or out of order, malformed identifiers, missing tenant or executor), duplicate names (409) on create and on rename, illegal transitions, updating a paused policy, findings that are inconsistent (a reference that is a sentence, an unknown severity, a patch announced in the future, applied before it was announced, a waiver that is free text, in the past or longer than a year), a finding for a policy that is not the tenant's, tenant isolation, limits of the list, and the absence of DELETE, with RFC 7807 error_code assertions. It files everything under its own generated tenant id (pchOrganisationId). A waiver running out by itself, and the race of simultaneous reports of one patch, are proved by the unit tests and by the platform smoke (patch-smoke).
